latest_release.body:
## 💥 Breaking changes

- Disallow mixed string \<=> numeric arithmetic in eager (#30071)

## 🚀 Performance improvements

- Limit the memory of buckets sorted ahead in the sort flush (#30297)
- Make file readers wait for spills while over the memory budget (#30296)
- Count unspilled frames in the memory estimate right away (#30295)
- Simplify more boolean expressions and drop redundant null checks (#30293)
- Wait for spills while over the out-of-core memory budget (#30294)
- Lower the default out-of-core prefetch fraction to 0.5 (#30292)
- Aggregate unique and n\_unique in the streaming group-by itself (#30281)
- Return freed memory to the OS right away while out-of-core data is spilled (#30280)
- Gather `List(Array)` and `Array` columns without per-row slices (#30278)
- Evaluate the streaming window node out of core (#30282)
- Avoid deep copies when building a DataFrame from flat dataclasses (#30275)
- Sort the window partitions by each order key instead of their row encoding (#30277)
- Scan the haystack for a single needle in `is_in` (#30276)
- Prefer fixed-width columns when only the row count is needed (#30274)
- Native gather for List arrays (#30019)
- Evaluate windows in filter predicates in the streaming window node (#30272)
- Don't busy-wait in RAYON.block\_on (#30259)
- Encode nested Parquet levels directly from the level buffers (#30251)
- Reduce memory of CSV scans on wide rows (#30165)
- Avoid quadratic JSON serialization of nested lists and maps (#30203)
- Skip the gather when exploding lists without nulls (#30234)
- Speed up writing nested Parquet columns (#30245)
- Don't keep whole parquet string dictionaries alive for a few selected rows (#30248)
- Set default spill compression level to 1 (#30237)
- Reuse zstd contexts in compression and avoid memcpys (#30233)
- Remove repeated and scalar ordering keys before the sort rewrites (#30231)
- Remove repeated keys from by's (#30095)
- Keep only one guessed unique key per join order leaf (#30191)
- Don't let extra join keys shrink an estimate once one key is unique (#30190)
- Reduce binary size of asof join with `by` keys (#30192)
- Reduce binary size of SQL visitors and parallel group-by collect (#30171)
- Push as-of join key filters to the right input (#30123)
- Drop null as-of right keys with a parallel filter before the join node (#30125)
- Keep as-of nearest join state small (#30126)
- Explode lists in group\_by aggregations without a per-group apply (#30020)
- Streaming OOC group-by with shuffles (#29911)
- Drop scalar ordering keys in the optimizer (#30063)
- Merge union inputs that scan files of the same kind into one multi-file scan (#30056)
- Use the streaming scalar window for std, var and combined reductions in `over` (#30066)
- Limit the bytes of local CSV and NDJSON files read at once in multi-file scans (#30055)
- Check the matched flag of join keys in the table entry before the bitset (#30067)
- Track matched build rows of all join tables in a bitset (#30050)
- Add dedicated list gather kernels (#30049)
- Emit unmatched build rows of single-key joins in row order (#30037)
- Use `TopK` for sorts sliced at a nonzero offset (#29989)
- Add constant folding for more datetime ops (#30016)
- Rewrite the sum of a column plus a literal to a sum and a count of the column (#30011)
- Push predicates through order-keeping columns (#30007)
- Fix dead early exit in `coalesce` (#30013)
- Count distinct non-null values in SQL with one group-by in the streaming engine (#30009)
- Skip parquet row groups with the running top-k threshold (#30006)
- Keep decompressed plain string pages as the string data buffer (#29984)
- Fix some in-memory filter regressions (#29988)
- Decompress snappy and zstd parquet pages without zeroing the buffer (#29980)
- Speed up `str.len_chars` (#29972)
- Speed up `str.replace` for patterns that end in `.*$` (#29971)
- Use the Parquet string prefilter for literal `str.contains` and SQL `LIKE` (#29953)
- Keep single-chunk output when filtering wide

detail.readme:
Documentation: Python - Rust - Node.js - R - SQL | Agents: Skill - MCP | User guide | Discord

## Polars: Extremely fast Query Engine for DataFrames and SQL Polars is an analytical query engine written in Rust. Write your queries with the DataFrame API, in SQL, or mix both: they run through the same optimizer and the same engine. It is designed to be fast, easy to use and expressive. Key features are: - **Fast**: written from the ground up in Rust with multi-threaded, vectorized (SIMD) execution - **Spill to disk**: Operations that exceed available RAM can spill to disk - **Expressive API**: compose complex queries with powerful expressions - **Extensible**: extend Polars natively with custom code through [I/O and Expression plugins](https://docs.pola.rs/user-guide/plugins/) - **GPU support**: optionally accelerate queries on NVIDIA GPUs - **Interoperable**: uses the [Apache Arrow Columnar Format](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/Columnar.html) for zero-copy data sharing To learn more, read the [user guide](https://docs.pola.rs/). ## Polars in action ### DataFrame API Queries are composed from expressions or SQL. This lazy query gets optimized out of the box and runs in parallel across all available cores: ```python import polars as pl df = ( pl.scan_parquet("orders.parquet") .filter(pl.col("status") == "shipped") .group_by("customer_id") .agg( pl.col("amount").sum().alias("total"), pl.len().alias("n_orders"), ) .sort("total", descending=True) .collect() ) ``` ### SQL ```python import polars as pl df = pl.sql(""" WITH totals AS ( SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total, COUNT(*) AS n_orders FROM read_parquet('orders.parquet') WHERE status = 'shipped' GROUP BY customer_id ) SELECT c.name, t.total, t.n_orders, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY t.total DESC) AS rank FROM totals t JOIN read_parquet('customers.parquet') c USING (customer_id) ORDER BY t.total DESC """).collect() ``` ### Mix both DataFrames and LazyFrames in scope can be queried by name, and the result of a SQL query is a regular `LazyFrame`, so you can switch between SQL and expressions freely: ```python orders = pl.scan_parquet("orders.parquet") df = ( pl.sql("SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id") .filter(pl.col("total") > 1_000) .collect() ) ``` Read more in the [SQL user guide](https://docs.pola.rs/user-guide/sql/intro/). ## Performance Polars is very fast. In fact, it is one of the best performing query engines available, for both DataFrame and SQL workloads. See the [PDS-H benchmarks](https://www.pola.rs/benchmarks.html) results. ## Installation ### Python Install the latest Polars version with: ```sh pip install polars ``` See the [User Guide](https://docs.pola.rs/user-guide/installation/#feature-flags) for more details on optional dependencies
Compile Polars from source If you want a bleeding edge release you should compile Polars from source. Advanced users can also compile for maximum performance for their architecture. This can be done by going through the following steps in sequence: 1. Install the latest [Rust compiler](https://www.rust-lang.org/tools/install) 2. Install [maturin](https://maturin.rs/): `pip install maturin` 3. `cd py-polars` and choose one of the following: - `make build`, slow binary with debug assertions and limited symbols, fast compile times - `make build-debug`, same as `make build`, but with all symbols, produces large binaries - `make build-release`, fast binary without debug assertions, minimal debug symbols, long compile times - `make build-nodebug-release`, same as build-release but without any debug symbols, slightly faster to compile - `make build-debug-release`, same as build-release but with full debug symbols, slightly slower to compile - `make build-dist-release`, fastest binary, extreme compile times By default the binary is compiled with optimizations turned on for a modern CPU. Specify `LTS_CPU=1` with the command if your CPU is older and does not support e.g. AVX2. Note that the Rust crate implementing the Python bindings is called `py-polars` to distinguish from the wrapped Rust crate `polars` itself. However, both the Python package and the Python module are named `polars`, so you can `pip install polars` and `import polars`.
Check the [Installation guide](https://docs.pola.rs/user-guide/installation/) for more advanced installations. For example when you expect more than 2^32 (~4.2 billion) rows, run on an old CPU (e.g. dating from before 2011), or on an `x86-64` build of Python on Apple Silicon under Rosetta. ## Contributing Want to contribute? Read our [contributing guide](https://docs.pola.rs/development/contributing/) and check the issue tracker for accepted issues. Contributors new to the codebase can look for the `good first issue` label to get familiar with the project. You can [join the Polars Discord server](https://discord.gg/4UfP5cfBE7) for any help along the way. ## Distributed Polars Running into hardware limitations executing your queries? Read how you can [horizontally scale your Polars query on a cluster](https://docs.nanook.pola.rs/). ## License Polars is licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE) (SPDX: `MIT`).
